regions.text: いふ語によつて表現され、目々必然と結合して自由の意味を取つた場合には、みづからの語が用ひられる。

quote.translation: When causal contingency means indeterminate spontaneity, Japanese expresses it with the word onozukara, and when it is joined with teleological necessity and takes on the meaning of freedom, Japanese uses the word mizukara.

regions.text: 「今さびしきすまひ、一間のいほりぷプからこれを愛す。

quote.translation: "Now I love my lonely dwelling, my hut of a single room, of myself (mizukara).

regions.text: おのづから都に出でて、身の乞匂となれる事を恥づといへどもがへりてここたをる時は他の俗感にはする事をあはれむ』（方丈記）。

quote.translation: When on occasion (onozukara) I go out to the capital I am ashamed to have become a beggar, yet when I return and stay here I pity others for running after the dust of the world" (Hōjōki).

regions.text: なほ「おのづから」といふ語は「自然を意味し、その結果として却つて因果約偶然に對立する場合もある。

quote.translation: The word onozukara can also mean "nature", and in that case, on the contrary, it can stand opposed to causal contingency.

regions.text: しかし、その時には半面に於て目々偶然を意味する限り、自然と偶然との合置したものを表現してあると考ふべきである。

quote.translation: Insofar as it then also means teleological contingency, however, we should think of it as expressing a union of nature and chance.

regions.text: 「理想特輯壁入生觀の哲學」中の「我が人生製二日二貫）では特にこの意味ですなはち自然をして因果前偶然に對立する意味で「おのづから」の語を用ひて置いた。

quote.translation: In "My View of Life" (p. 242), in the special issue of Risō on "The Philosophy of the View of Life", I used the word onozukara in this sense in particular, that is, in the sense of "nature" standing opposed to causal contingency.

regions.text: 「わざと習ひまねばねども少しもかどあらむ人の、耳にも目にもとまる事じかんに多かるべし。

quote.translation: "Even without deliberately learning and imitating, the things that catch the ear and the eye of anyone with a little talent must naturally (jinen ni) be many.

regions.text: さるままにはまんなを走り書きて、さるまじきどちの女ぶみになかば過ぎて書きすくめたる、あなうたてこの方のたをやかならましかばと見ゆかし。

quote.translation: And so she dashes off mana, and in letters between women, where it is out of place, she crams them in until more than half the page is filled; how distasteful, and one wishes she were gentler in this respect.

regions.text: 心地にはきしも思はさらめど、おのプからこはごはしき弊に讀みなされなどしつつこをさらびた、り』税氏物語存水）。

quote.translation: Though in her heart she may not mean it so, it comes of itself (onozukara) to be read out in a stiff voice, and seems affected" (Genji monogatari, Hahakigi).

regions.text: この場合、「自然に」とおのづからとが全然同意義であること

quote.translation: That in this passage jinen ni and onozukara have exactly the same meaning rests on the same Ground as Plato's treating nature and chance as of one kind (see p. 78).
